description: This pie chart, from the paper “Evaluation of Speaker Anonymization on Emotional Speech,” visually represents the distribution of six distinct emotional categories: Frustration, Neutral, Anger, Sadness, Happiness, and Excitement. The chart is divided into six colored slices, each labeled with its corresponding emotion and percentage value. The largest slice is Frustration at 25.1%, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. The remaining four categories—Anger (14.9%), Sadness (14.7%), Excitement (14.1%), and Happiness (8.1%)—are all smaller, with Happiness being the smallest segment. Each slice is distinctly colored: Frustration is light blue, Neutral is medium blue, Anger is yellow, Sadness is orange, Excitement is red, and Happiness is a lighter shade of blue. The percentages are clearly printed inside each slice, and the chart includes a legend (though not visible in this view, it would typically match the colors to the labels). The slices are arranged in a clockwise descending order of size, starting from the top with Frustration, followed by Neutral, then Anger, Sadness, Excitement, and finally Happiness at the bottom right.
